purpose: Stiripentol is used to help control seizures in people with a rare and serious type of epilepsy called Dravet syndrome. It is usually used together with other seizure medicines, especially valproate and clobazam. It is approved for children and adults who have been diagnosed with this condition.
how_it_works: Stiripentol works by calming down overexcited nerve activity in the brain that causes seizures. It does this mainly by boosting the effect of a natural calming chemical in your brain called GABA, which helps slow down abnormal electrical signals. It also helps other seizure medicines work better by slowing down how quickly your body breaks them down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include drowsiness or feeling very sleepy, loss of appetite, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, and unsteady walking or balance problems. Some children may also become irritable or have trouble sleeping. These effects are often related to the other seizure medicines being taken at the same time.
warnings: Talk to your doctor right away if you notice unusual behavior, mood changes, thoughts of self-harm, or signs of a serious liver problem like yellowing of the skin or eyes. This medicine can make you very drowsy, so avoid driving or operating heavy machinery. Never stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can make seizures worse. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, because stiripentol can interact with many drugs.
typical_dosing: The dose is usually based on your body weight and is taken two or three times a day with food. A common starting dose for children is around 50 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into multiple doses. Your doctor will slowly adjust the dose to find what works best for you while keeping side effects manageable. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
